textBlocks.text:
RESTAURANT VFX BUILD — 10-SECOND ONE-TAKE FPV USE THE UPLOADED REFERENCE IMAGE AS THE FINAL ARCHITECTURAL AND INTERIOR DESIGN TARGET ONLY.

The uploaded image represents the COMPLETED RESTAURANT AT THE END OF THE VIDEO.

It is NOT the starting state.

At 00:00, the restaurant interior is completely empty.

The video must show the restaurant being physically constructed from nothing during one continuous, extremely dynamic FPV camera shot.

By 00:10, the completed restaurant must match the uploaded reference as closely as possible.

Preserve the reference's: architecture, proportions, spatial layout, floor plan, ceiling geometry, furniture placement, materials, colors,
lighting design, bar/counter, seating, decorative elements, plants, wall treatments, windows and overall visual identity.

Do not redesign the restaurant.

Do not invent a different interior.

The uploaded image is the final destination.

CORE VISUAL CONCEPT

This is NOT a normal interior timelapse.

This is a high-end Hollywood VFX construction sequence.

The restaurant appears to be assembled by a violent invisible gravitational force.

Materials begin as loose physical components scattered beneath and around the empty space.

Then the entire interior enters a controlled state of reverse gravity / electromagnetic construction.

Massive objects violently launch upward.

Smaller components orbit around them.

Materials rotate through the air.

Architectural pieces accelerate toward their final positions.

Components collide, align and mechanically lock together.

Every major construction event creates: realistic impact dust tiny debris sparks from metal connections vibration secondary particles
subtle camera shake motion trails caused by extreme velocity realistic momentum physically believable collisions The effect must feel like
real architecture being assembled at impossible speed, not magical CGI.

ABSOLUTE CAMERA RULE

ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS CAMERA TAKE.

The entire 10 seconds must be captured by one uninterrupted FPV camera movement.

NO CUTS.

NO HIDDEN CUTS.

NO EDITS.

NO TRANSITIONS.

NO FADE.

NO TELEPORTATION.

NO CAMERA RESET.

NO DISCONTINUOUS POSITION CHANGES.

The camera must continuously travel through the same physical restaurant space from beginning to end.

The camera itself must feel physically present inside the construction.

Objects should pass extremely close to the lens.

The camera should sometimes narrowly avoid incoming objects by only a few centimeters.

Use aggressive:

FPV banking, barrel rolls, rapid pitch changes, speed ramps, dives, climbs, tight arcs, parallax passes and near-miss maneuvers.

However, the camera movement must remain physically continuous.

VISUAL LANGUAGE

Photorealistic luxury architectural commercial.

Hollywood VFX quality.

IMAX-scale realism.

14mm ultra-wide FPV lens.

High dynamic range.

Physically accurate global illumination.

Realistic reflections.

Realistic glass refraction.

Realistic brushed metal.

Realistic stone.

Realistic wood.

Realistic fabric.

Realistic polished floors.

Volumetric atmospheric light.

Subtle lens bloom.

Natural motion blur.

Realistic depth of field.

Fine dust particles.

Micro-debris.

Tiny floating particles catching the light.

Extremely detailed materials.

No artificial video-game appearance.

No plastic-looking CGI.

No fantasy environment.

The finished restaurant should look like a real architectural photograph.

IMPORTANT — CONSTRUCTION MUST HAVE A VISUAL HIERARCHY Do NOT assemble every object simultaneously.

The construction happens in large cinematic waves: STRUCTURE → ARCHITECTURE → FURNITURE → LIGHTING → DECORATION → FINAL DETAILS Large
objects dominate first.

Small objects appear only after the major structure is established.

This prevents visual clutter and keeps the construction readable.

00:00–00:01 — THE EMPTY SPACE

Begin inside the exact spatial environment represented by the reference image.

The restaurant is completely empty.

Only the bare architectural shell exists.

Bare concrete floor.

Bare structural walls.

Bare ceiling.

No furniture.

No lights.

No plants.

No decorations.

No bar.

No equipment.

No finished interior.

Camera flies approximately 20 cm above the floor at extremely high speed.

The empty room feels strangely still.

Then the floor begins vibrating.

Dust trembles.

Small pieces of gravel jump.

Metal fragments rotate.

Tiny screws begin floating upward.

A low-frequency physical vibration travels through the floor.

The camera accelerates directly into the disturbance.

00:01–00:02 — THE CONSTRUCTION VORTEX

Suddenly, hundreds of construction components violently launch upward.

Not randomly.

They begin forming a gigantic spiraling construction vortex around the camera.

Floor slabs.

Stone.

Wood.

Metal framing.

Glass.

Electrical components.

Ceiling pieces.

Architectural panels.

Everything rotates around a central invisible axis.

The camera flies directly through the vortex.

Large objects pass within centimeters of the lens.

The camera narrowly avoids a massive stone slab.

A steel frame rotates directly above the camera.

A cloud of dust explodes past the lens.

The construction vortex rapidly compresses toward the restaurant's final geometry.

00:02–00:03 — FLOOR + ARCHITECTURE LOCK

The camera dives toward the floor.

The finished flooring rapidly assembles beneath it.

Individual stone / wood / concrete / tile sections shoot upward and slide together with millimeter precision.

THUD.

First section locks.

THUD.

Second section locks.

Then dozens more rapidly connect in a wave traveling toward the camera.

At the same time: wall panels rise.

Architectural columns form.

Ceiling structures unfold.

Wood slats rotate into alignment.

Decorative architectural geometry snaps into place.

Every connection produces tiny realistic dust bursts and mechanical vibration.

The camera flies directly through the newly forming architecture.

00:03–00:04 — THE BAR EXPLODES INTO EXISTENCE The camera aggressively banks toward the main bar / counter.

This becomes the first major hero construction moment.

The bar structure launches upward from the floor.

Cabinet modules rotate.

Metal framework assembles.

Stone countertop flies horizontally through frame.

It rotates approximately 90 degrees.

Then:

SLAM.

It locks perfectly into place.

Shelves rise behind it.

Glass panels snap together.

Bottle shelves assemble.

Metal details attach.

The camera performs a tight FPV orbit around the rapidly forming bar.

The entire structure completes in less than one second.

A powerful pressure wave pushes dust away from the completed counter.

00:04–00:05 — FURNITURE STORM

The camera launches into the dining area.

Now the furniture construction begins.

Dozens of tables and chairs are initially visible as individual components flying through the environment.

But instead of appearing randomly: they travel along controlled curved trajectories, almost like they are being pulled by an invisible
magnetic field.

Chair legs rotate.

Frames assemble.

Seats lock.

Backrests snap into place.

Table legs rise.

Tabletops spin horizontally.

Tables land perfectly.

Entire rows of seating assemble in synchronized waves.

The camera flies directly between them.

One chair misses the lens by centimeters.

A tabletop rotates above the camera.

Another table locks into position directly behind the camera.

Everything follows the exact arrangement of the reference image.

00:05–00:06 — LIGHTING ACTIVATION WAVE

The camera suddenly pitches vertically upward.

The ceiling becomes the focus.

Pendant lights, track lights, chandeliers and LED elements rise into the frame.

Electrical cables rapidly connect.

Metal fixtures rotate.

Glass shades lock into position.

Then the lighting activates in a CHAIN REACTION.

One light turns on.

Then the next.

Then the next.

Then dozens simultaneously.

A warm illumination wave travels through the entire restaurant.

The environment changes from cold unfinished construction space into the finished luxurious atmosphere of the reference.

The camera dives back toward the dining area.

00:06–00:07 — ARCHITECTURAL DETAIL STORM

Now the small details begin assembling.

But they must behave like a controlled VFX particle system.

Plants rise from the floor.

Leaves unfold.

Decorative panels fly toward walls.

Mirrors rotate into position.

Artwork locks onto walls.

Shelves assemble.

Cushions land on seating.

Curtains drop.

Table settings rapidly appear.

Glassware rotates into position.

Small decorative objects orbit once around the camera before locking into their final locations.

Use elegant controlled trajectories rather than random flying objects.

The camera aggressively weaves through the storm.

Every object has realistic momentum.

00:07–00:08 — FINAL 10% / MAXIMUM VFX INTENSITY The restaurant is now approximately 90% complete.

The camera accelerates dramatically.

The remaining components suddenly begin moving much faster.

Hundreds of tiny architectural details fly through the room.

Metal particles.

Glass fragments.

Wood components.

Decorative elements.

Lighting details.

Furniture details.

Plants.

Small objects.

All converge toward their final positions.

The entire restaurant appears to be temporarily surrounded by a controlled swirling construction field.

The camera flies directly through its center.

Then—

EVERYTHING STOPS.

For approximately a fraction of a second, all remaining objects hang perfectly suspended in the air.

Absolute visual tension.

00:08–00:09 — GRAVITY SNAP

Gravity suddenly returns.

Everything suspended above the restaurant drops downward.

But instead of falling randomly, every component falls toward its exact final position.

Tables settle.

Chairs land.

Decorations drop.

Pendant lights stabilize.

Plants settle.

Final architectural elements descend.

Each object lands with a precise physical impact.

A synchronized wave of tiny dust bursts travels across the restaurant.

The camera performs a rapid backward dive.

00:09–00:10 — THE FINAL REVEAL

The final remaining architectural component falls into place.

MASSIVE FINAL IMPACT.

A subtle circular dust shockwave expands across the floor.

The camera rockets backward and upward.

The entire completed restaurant is revealed.

All lights are fully active.

All materials are finished.

All furniture is perfectly positioned.

The environment is completely clean and premium.

The camera slows into a beautiful cinematic architectural hero shot.

The final composition should closely resemble the uploaded reference image.

The transformation should feel like:

EMPTY SPACE → IMPOSSIBLE CONSTRUCTION → COMPLETE LUXURY RESTAURANT The final frame must look like a real professional architectural
photograph.

PHYSICS REQUIREMENTS

Every object must obey believable physics.

Objects have weight.

Objects have inertia.

Objects accelerate and decelerate.

Large objects move slower than small objects.

Heavy stone and metal must feel heavy.

Glass must feel fragile.

Wood must have realistic mass.

Furniture must not float unnaturally.

Objects cannot pass through each other.

Objects cannot merge together.

Objects cannot duplicate.

Objects cannot randomly disappear.

No object may teleport.

No object may morph from one shape into another.

Each object must visibly travel from its origin to its destination.

CAMERA / VFX INTERACTION

The camera must interact with the construction.

Objects should pass extremely close to the lens.

Particles should occasionally hit the lens.

Dust should briefly obscure the image.

Fast-moving objects should create strong motion blur.

Large impacts should produce subtle physical camera shake.

Air pressure from large objects should move nearby dust.

The camera should react naturally to nearby impacts.

Use aggressive but believable FPV movement.

The camera should feel like a real drone flying through an active construction site.

REFERENCE MATCHING RULE

The reference image is the single source of truth for the final restaurant.

Do not invent: new furniture, new walls, new windows, new architectural shapes, new colors, new lighting fixtures, new decorations, new
layouts, new signage, or additional rooms.

If an object is not visible or clearly implied by the reference, do not introduce it unnecessarily.

The AI must prioritize reference accuracy over adding visual complexity.

FINAL NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS

NO CUTS.

NO HIDDEN CUTS.

NO CAMERA TELEPORTATION.

NO CAMERA RESET.

NO TIME JUMPS.

NO MORPHING.

NO MAGICALLY SPAWNED OBJECTS.

NO RANDOM OBJECTS.

NO DUPLICATED OBJECTS.

NO FLOATING FURNITURE.

NO IMPOSSIBLE PHYSICS.

NO OBJECT INTERSECTIONS.

NO MELTING MATERIALS.

NO RUBBER-LIKE METAL.

NO PLASTIC-LOOKING WOOD.

NO CGI-LOOKING GLASS.

NO DISTORTED ARCHITECTURE.

NO RANDOM ROOM CHANGES.

NO SCI-FI BUILDING.

NO FUTURISTIC HOLOGRAMS.

NO TEXT.

NO CAPTIONS.

NO WATERMARKS.

NO LOGOS UNLESS THEY ARE PRESENT IN THE REFERENCE.

NO PEOPLE UNLESS PRESENT IN THE REFERENCE.

NO RANDOM CAMERA CUTS.

NO SUDDEN CHANGE OF LENS.

NO CHANGE OF ENVIRONMENT.

NO CHANGE OF ARCHITECTURAL STYLE.

The entire sequence must feel like one physically continuous impossible construction event captured by one FPV camera.

The final restaurant must look real enough that the viewer could believe the entire interior was actually assembled around the camera.
